rv.q: With some reservations, this musical production of The Great Gatsby can be recommended for those individuals who are looking for something different.
Sadly, the five-star production values are wrapped around a barely two-star adaptation of the novel itself.

There's more than enough going for this production that, if you're a fan of the novel and lavish musicals, Old Sport, you should have no reservations about following that green light that so obsesses Jay Gatsby all the way to Playhouse Square.
Honestly, this "Gatsby” rivals another recent extravaganza, “Moulin Rouge,” for thrilling artistic spectacle.
This version of 'The Great Gatsby' works best if one just forgets about the book from whence it came.

This adaptation is a re-imagining of everything from major plot points, famous lines, and well-known characters that would not be recognizable as embodying much of the spirit or the letter of Fitzgerald's masterpiece.

And this show, which is running through May 31 at the Benedum Center in Downtown Pittsburgh as part of the Pittsburgh Cultural Trust's PNC Broadway in Pittsburgh Series, has glimmers of fun and heart.

While visually stunning and brimming with high-caliber talent, The Great Gatsby musical struggled to translate the novel's narrative into a compelling stage experience on Wednesday night at the Music Hall at Fair Park.
It's not a hard show to sit through by any means, thanks to the fine voices and the efficient staging.
The result is a production that excels in style while falling short on substance.
But in the end, it seems to be about nothing so much as Jay Gatsby’s (Jake David Smith) parties and what they wore—and that is simply not enough to merit two-and-a-half hours of stage time.

cn.t: A lavish spectacle with stunning costumes and sets, but the musical adaptation falls short of capturing Fitzgerald's novel's depth, favoring style over substance with a forgettable score.
